recipe.name: Masala Idli
steps: Let the cooked idlis cool until firm, then cut them into bite-sized cubes. Chop onion, tomato, green chilli, ginger and coriander separately.
Heat oil in a wide pan, splutter mustard and curry leaves, then cook onion, ginger and chilli for 4–5 minutes until the onion softens.
Add tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and salt. Cook uncovered for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until the tomato becomes a thick coating rather than a watery sauce.
Add the idli cubes and toss gently for 2–3 minutes to coat all sides without breaking them. Cover for one minute so the centres heat through.
Scatter coriander over the hot idli and serve at once. Using cooled idlis helps each cube hold its shape in the masala.
tips: This is a useful fresh preparation for cooled idlis, but the cubes must be heated fully before serving.
recipe.passiveTime: No passive preparation required when cooked idlis are ready.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Oats Idli
steps: Dry-roast rolled oats over low heat for 3–4 minutes until fragrant, cool and pulse into a coarse flour. Roast semolina separately for 2 minutes without browning.
Heat oil, splutter mustard and curry leaves, then cook grated carrot for 2 minutes. Mix the oat flour, semolina, carrot tempering, curd, measured water and salt into a thick spoonable batter.
Rest 10 minutes so the oats hydrate. Set a steamer to boil and lightly oil idli moulds. If the batter has become stiff, loosen with a small splash of water.
Immediately before steaming, stir in fruit salt gently until the batter lightens. Fill moulds three-quarters full and steam for 12–15 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Rest for 2 minutes, unmould and serve warm with coconut chutney. Add fruit salt only once the steamer is ready, or the bubbles escape before cooking.
tips: Fruit salt is a leavening ingredient; use plain unflavoured fruit salt with no egg-derived additives.
recipe.passiveTime: Rest the batter for 10 minutes before steaming.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Ragi Idli
steps: Wash and soak idli rice, urad dal and fenugreek for 5 hours. Drain and grind with most of the measured water until smooth and airy.
Whisk finger millet flour with the remaining water to remove dry lumps, then fold it into the ground batter. Cover loosely and ferment overnight until risen and gently tangy.
Stir in salt without knocking out the air. Brush idli moulds lightly with oil and pour batter to about three-quarters of each cup; bring steamer water to a full boil.
Steam for 12–15 minutes until the brown idlis spring back and a skewer comes out clean. Rest two minutes before unmoulding to avoid tearing the soft crumb.
Serve three warm ragi idlis per person with coconut chutney. Keep the batter thick enough to hold air; adding too much water makes flat idlis.
tips: Ragi flour darkens the idlis naturally; it does not mean they are overcooked.

recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Poha Idli
steps: Rinse poha quickly, drain and let it soften for 5 minutes. Pulse it into a coarse paste rather than a completely smooth liquid.
Dry-roast semolina for 2–3 minutes without browning. Mix it with poha, curd, measured water and salt into a thick batter; rest 15 minutes so both grains hydrate.
Set the steamer water to boil and oil the idli moulds. Stir the batter; add a small splash of water only if it is too stiff to spoon.
Just before steaming, fold in fruit salt gently and fill moulds three-quarters full. Steam for 12–15 minutes until a skewer comes out clean; do not open the lid in the first 10 minutes.
Rest the idlis for 2 minutes, unmould and serve three soft poha idlis per person with coconut chutney. Add fruit salt only when the steamer is ready.
tips: A little coarse poha texture makes these idlis softer than using only semolina.
recipe.passiveTime: Rest the poha-semolina batter for 15 minutes.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Mini Tiffin
steps: Soak idli rice, urad dal and fenugreek for 5 hours, grind with enough of the measured water to a smooth thick batter, and ferment overnight until risen. Add half the salt; reserve half the batter for mini idlis and thin the rest slightly for dosas.
Oil mini-idli moulds, fill them three-quarters with batter and steam over boiling water for 8–10 minutes. Rest briefly and unmould; make about twelve mini idlis.

For pongal, rinse short-grain rice and moong dal, then simmer with about 360 ml of the measured water until very soft, 20–25 minutes. Heat 25 g ghee, toast cumin and crushed pepper, then fold into the soft rice-dal mixture with a pinch of salt.

For kesari, roast semolina in 20 g ghee until fragrant. Bring 250 ml of the measured water with sugar to a boil, add roasted semolina slowly while stirring, and cook until thick and glossy. Fry cashews in 10 g ghee and scatter on top.
Heat a flat griddle and make four small dosas from the reserved batter, using the measured oil around the edges; cook until lightly crisp and golden. Warm the prepared sambar.

Arrange three mini idlis, one small dosa, a spoonful of pongal and a separate spoonful of sweet kesari on each of four plates. Add coconut chutney and sambar alongside so the sweet portion stays distinct.
tips: Keep the sweet kesari in its own section so it does not soak up sambar.
recipe.passiveTime: Soak rice and urad dal for 5 hours, then ferment the batter overnight.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

hi.Quantities serve four adults. Check the: मात्राएँ चार वयस्कों के लिए हैं। हर चरण में पकने के संकेत जाँचें और स्वाद के अनुसार मसाला बदलें। जैन उपयुक्तता आपके परिवार की सामग्री संबंधी नियमों पर निर्भर है।
hi.Soak idli rice, urad dal and fenugreek f: इडली चावल, उड़द दाल और मेथी 5 घंटे भिगोकर नापे पानी में से जरूरत भर से चिकना गाढ़ा घोल पीसें और रात भर फूलने तक खमीर उठाएँ। आधा नमक मिलाएँ; आधा घोल मिनी इडली के लिए रखें और बाकी डोसे के लिए थोड़ा पतला करें।
hi.Oil mini-idli moulds, fill them three-qu: मिनी-इडली साँचे में तेल लगाएँ, तीन-चौथाई घोल भरें और उबलते पानी की भाप में 8–10 मिनट पकाएँ। थोड़ा रखकर निकालें; लगभग बारह मिनी इडली बनाएँ।
hi.For pongal, rinse short-grain rice and m: पोंगल के लिए छोटे चावल और मूँग दाल धोकर नापे पानी में से लगभग 360 मिली में 20–25 मिनट बहुत नरम पकाएँ। 25 ग्राम घी में जीरा और कुटी काली मिर्च भूनकर नरम चावल-दाल में चुटकी नमक के साथ मिलाएँ।
hi.For kesari, roast semolina in 20 g ghee: केसरी के लिए सूजी 20 ग्राम घी में सुगंध आने तक भूनें। नापे पानी में से 250 मिली चीनी के साथ उबालें, भुनी सूजी धीरे चलाते हुए डालें और गाढ़ा चमकदार होने तक पकाएँ। काजू 10 ग्राम घी में तलकर ऊपर डालें।
hi.Heat a flat griddle and make four small: सपाट तवा गरम कर बचे घोल से चार छोटे डोसे बनाएँ, नापा तेल किनारों पर डालें; हल्के कुरकुरे सुनहरे होने तक पकाएँ। तैयार सांभर गरम करें।
hi.Arrange three mini idlis, one small dosa: चार प्लेटों में हर एक पर तीन मिनी इडली, एक छोटा डोसा, थोड़ा पोंगल और अलग थोड़ा मीठा केसरी रखें। नारियल चटनी और सांभर साथ में दें ताकि मीठा हिस्सा अलग रहे।
hi.Keep the sweet kesari in its own section: मीठे केसरी को अलग रखें ताकि सांभर उसमें न सोखे।
hi.Soak rice and urad dal for 5 hours, then: चावल और उड़द दाल 5 घंटे भिगोकर घोल रात भर खमीर उठाएँ।

recipe.name: Chow Chow Bath
steps: Divide the semolina into two equal portions. Roast each separately over low heat until fragrant but not brown; keep the savory and sweet batches apart.
For khara bath, heat oil, splutter mustard and curry leaves, then soften chopped onion and chilli. Add diced carrot and peas and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in 450 ml boiling water and salt, then slowly add one semolina portion while stirring. Cover and cook 4–5 minutes until soft and moist; fluff and keep warm.

For kesari bath, boil the remaining water with sugar. Stir in the second roasted semolina portion gradually and cook until thick, then fold in ghee, cardamom and cashews toasted in a little of that ghee.
Spoon equal mounds of savory khara bath and sweet kesari bath side by side on four plates. Serve warm, keeping the two flavors distinct until eating.
tips: The two semolina dishes share a plate but are cooked in separate pans.
recipe.passiveTime: No long resting time; prepare savory and sweet halves separately.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

hi.No long resting time; prepare savory and: लंबा विराम नहीं; नमकीन और मीठे भाग अलग बनाएँ।

recipe.name: Tomato Bath
steps: Dry-roast semolina for 4 minutes until fragrant but pale, then spread it on a plate to cool.
Heat the measured oil in a wide pan, splutter mustard and curry leaves, then soften chopped onion, chilli and ginger for 4–5 minutes over medium heat.
Add chopped tomato and turmeric to the softened aromatics and cook for 6–8 minutes until the tomatoes collapse into a thick red base; toast cashews separately.
Add 650 ml boiling water and the measured salt. Sprinkle in roasted semolina slowly while stirring, cover and cook 4–5 minutes until the grains are soft but not gluey.
Switch off the heat, fluff gently and finish with chopped coriander. Divide into four bowls and serve warm; avoid packing down the grains. Top each bowl with the toasted cashews.
tips: Cook the tomatoes down before adding water for a concentrated tomato flavor.
recipe.passiveTime: No passive preparation required.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Arisi Upma
steps: Rinse the broken rice and toor dal separately, then drain thoroughly. Keep the grains coarse; they should not be ground to flour.
Heat the measured oil in a wide pan, splutter mustard and curry leaves, then soften chopped onion, chilli and ginger for 4–5 minutes over medium heat.
Add cumin and drained toor dal to the softened onion mixture and stir for 2 minutes; the dal should be coated in the tempering before the rice goes in.
Stir in the broken rice, 800 ml hot water and salt. Cover and cook on low heat for 18–22 minutes, stirring once, until rice and dal are tender yet the grains remain distinct.
Switch off the heat, fluff gently and finish with chopped coriander. Divide into four bowls and serve warm; avoid packing down the grains. Fold in the fresh grated coconut just before serving.
tips: Use coarse broken rice, not rice flour, for the traditional granular texture.
recipe.passiveTime: No passive preparation required.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Rava Kichadi
steps: Dry-roast semolina for 4 minutes until aromatic without browning, then set aside. Dice carrot small so it cooks at the same pace as the peas.
Heat the measured oil in a wide pan, splutter mustard and curry leaves, then soften chopped onion, chilli and ginger for 4–5 minutes over medium heat.
Add carrot, peas and turmeric to the softened onion mixture and cook for 4 minutes. Fry cashews in ghee separately until pale golden.
Pour in 850 ml boiling water and salt, then stir in roasted semolina in a steady stream. Cover over low heat for 5–6 minutes until the kichadi is soft and moist rather than dry and crumbly.
Switch off the heat, fluff gently and finish with chopped coriander. Divide into four bowls and serve warm; avoid packing down the grains. Fold in the ghee and scatter toasted cashews on top.
tips: The extra water keeps hotel-style kichadi softer than ordinary upma.

recipe.name: Oats Upma
steps: Dry-toast rolled oats over low heat for 3 minutes until fragrant, then remove them promptly so the flakes stay separate.
Heat the measured oil in a wide pan, splutter mustard and curry leaves, then soften chopped onion, chilli and ginger for 4–5 minutes over medium heat.
Add diced carrot and peas to the softened onion mixture and cook for 4 minutes, adding a spoonful of water only if the pan catches.
Add the toasted oats, 430 ml hot water and salt. Cover for 3–4 minutes until the flakes soften but retain shape; stir gently rather than mashing them.
Switch off the heat, fluff gently and finish with chopped coriander. Divide into four bowls and serve warm; avoid packing down the grains. Finish with the measured lemon juice.

recipe.name: Quinoa Upma
steps: Rinse quinoa in a fine sieve under running water for at least 30 seconds to remove its bitter coating, then drain well.
Heat the measured oil in a wide pan, splutter mustard and curry leaves, then soften chopped onion, chilli and ginger for 4–5 minutes over medium heat.
Dice carrot and beans small, then cook them with peas in the softened onion mixture for 4 minutes so they finish cooking with the quinoa.
Stir in the drained quinoa, 580 ml hot water and salt. Cover over low heat for 15–18 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the tiny white tails appear; rest covered 5 minutes.
Switch off the heat, fluff gently and finish with chopped coriander. Divide into four bowls and serve warm; avoid packing down the grains. Finish with the measured lemon juice.
tips: Fully cooked quinoa shows a tiny white germ ring and remains separate, not translucent like tapioca.
recipe.passiveTime: No passive preparation required.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Foxtail Millet Upma
steps: Rinse foxtail millet two or three times and drain well. Leave it in the sieve while preparing the vegetables so the grains do not become waterlogged.
Heat the measured oil in a wide pan, splutter mustard and curry leaves, then soften chopped onion, chilli and ginger for 4–5 minutes over medium heat.
Dice carrot and beans small, then cook with peas in the softened onion mixture for 4 minutes until the vegetables are bright but not mushy.
Add drained millet, 650 ml hot water and salt. Cover and simmer 12–15 minutes until the grains are tender and the water absorbed; rest covered for 5 minutes before fluffing.
Switch off the heat, fluff gently and finish with chopped coriander. Divide into four bowls and serve warm; avoid packing down the grains. Finish with the measured lemon juice.
tips: Resting the covered millet separates the small grains without drying them.

recipe.name: Dadpe Pohe
steps: Use thin poha that softens without cooking. Put it in a wide bowl, briefly sprinkle with a little water if very dry, and gently separate the flakes with fingertips; do not soak or boil it.
Finely chop onion, green chilli and coriander. Mix them with fresh coconut, lemon juice, salt and sugar, then toss through the poha until evenly distributed.
Heat oil in a small pan, splutter mustard and curry leaves, and pour the hot tempering over the poha. Toss once more without crushing the flakes.
Cover the bowl for 10 minutes so the onion, coconut and lemon moisture softens the flattened rice. Taste a flake; it should be pliable yet light, not wet or mushy.
Fluff with a fork and serve in four bowls at room temperature. This is an uncooked poha preparation apart from the brief tempering.
tips: Do not use thick poha that needs cooking; dadpe pohe relies on thin flakes softening under cover.
recipe.passiveTime: Rest the assembled poha covered for 10 minutes.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Chura Matar
steps: Rinse thick chura briefly in a sieve, drain 10 minutes and fluff. It should soften but retain distinct broad flakes; never leave it immersed in water.
Heat half the ghee in a wide pan, toast cumin, then soften chopped onion, ginger and chilli. Add peas and cook for 5–6 minutes until tender and bright green.
Pour in milk and simmer briefly. Fold in softened chura and salt, then cover over very low heat for 3–4 minutes so the flakes absorb the pea flavors without becoming yellow or mashed.
Switch off heat, add remaining ghee and lemon juice, and toss gently. Let stand covered for 2 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Scatter coriander and serve warm in four bowls. This Banarasi dish should remain pale, moist and strongly studded with peas, unlike turmeric-yellow poha.
tips: Use fresh winter peas when available; this preparation showcases peas rather than spice powder.
recipe.passiveTime: Drain rinsed poha for 10 minutes before cooking.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Chirer Pulao
steps: Rinse thick chire in a sieve and drain for 10 minutes. Fluff gently so the flattened rice softens without collapsing into a paste.
Dice carrot and potato small. Heat half the oil, fry cashews until golden and raisins until plump, then lift both out before they burn.
Heat remaining oil with cumin, cook carrot, potato and peas for 6–8 minutes until tender. Add turmeric, sugar and salt, stirring to coat the vegetables.
Fold in drained chire and cook covered on low heat for 3–4 minutes until warmed through. Stir very gently so the flakes stay distinct.
Return cashews and raisins, scatter coriander and serve warm. The little sweetness and nuts distinguish Bengali chirer pulao from a plain savory poha.
tips: Fry the raisins briefly: they plump in seconds and burn if left in hot oil.

recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Aval Nanachathu
steps: Rinse the flattened rice very briefly and drain thoroughly. Leave it 5 minutes so the flakes soften without disintegrating; use a medium thickness rather than the very thin uncooked-poha type.
Dissolve grated jaggery in the measured warm water, strain if gritty, and stir in cardamom and a tiny pinch of salt. This should be a light coating, not a pool of syrup.
Toss the softened aval with fresh grated coconut and the jaggery liquid. Fold gently until every flake is lightly coated.
Cover for 10 minutes so the coconut and jaggery moisture penetrates the aval. Slice bananas just before serving to avoid browning.
Divide into four bowls and top with banana slices. Serve at room temperature; this is a moist, sweet breakfast, not a cooked porridge.
tips: Adjust softness with a tablespoon of water only if the flakes remain hard after resting.
recipe.passiveTime: Rest the dressed flattened rice for 10 minutes.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Rava Chilla
steps: Whisk semolina, curd, measured water and salt into a thick spoonable batter. Cover for 15 minutes so the semolina hydrates evenly.
Finely chop onion, green chilli and coriander and grate carrot. Fold them into the batter; if the semolina has thickened too much, add a small splash of water so it spreads with a spoon.
Heat a non-stick or seasoned griddle over medium heat and brush with a little measured oil. Spoon one-eighth of the batter into a small thick round and spread gently.
Cook 2–3 minutes until the underside is golden and the top nearly set. Flip carefully and cook another 2 minutes until the centre is firm with no raw semolina.
Make eight chillas and serve two per person with prepared green chutney. Keep the heat moderate so the vegetables and middle cook before the outside browns.
tips: Let the batter hydrate before judging its thickness; dry semolina keeps absorbing water.
recipe.passiveTime: Rest the semolina-curd batter for 15 minutes.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Oats Chilla
steps: Whisk oat flour, curd, measured water and salt to a smooth, thick batter. Rest 10 minutes so the oat flour hydrates instead of forming dry pockets on the griddle.
Grate carrot and finely chop onion, chilli and coriander. Fold them and cumin into the batter; add a tablespoon of water only if it no longer spreads with a spoon.
Heat a lightly oiled flat griddle over medium heat. Spoon one-eighth of the batter into a medium round and spread gently to about 5 mm thick.
Cook 2–3 minutes until the base is golden and the edges look set. Turn and cook a further 2 minutes until the middle is firm and the vegetables are tender.
Make eight chillas, using the measured oil a little at a time. Serve two per person with green chutney while warm.
tips: Oat batter thickens as it rests; adjust only at cooking time.

recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Tomato Besan Chilla
steps: Whisk gram flour, turmeric and salt with measured water until no lumps remain. Leave it 5 minutes so the flour hydrates; this omelette-style pancake contains no eggs.
Finely chop tomato, onion, chilli and coriander. Fold them into the batter, distributing the tomato evenly without crushing it into a watery puree.
Heat a seasoned griddle over medium heat and brush with a little measured oil. Pour one-eighth of the batter and spread into a thin but sturdy round.
Cook 2–3 minutes until the base sets and browns lightly. Turn carefully and cook another 2 minutes until the gram flour is fully cooked and the centre is no longer wet.
Make eight pancakes and serve two per person, folded with green chutney. Keep the heat moderate so the tomato pieces cook without scorching the base.
tips: Despite its name, Mumbai tomato omelette is traditionally an eggless gram-flour pancake.
recipe.passiveTime: Rest the gram-flour batter for 5 minutes.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Mitha Pudla
steps: Dissolve grated jaggery in half the measured warm water and strain away any grit. Whisk whole wheat flour, cardamom and salt in a bowl.
Pour in the jaggery liquid and remaining water gradually, whisking until a smooth pourable batter forms. Rest for 15 minutes so the flour hydrates; stir again before cooking.
Heat a flat griddle over medium-low heat and brush with a little ghee. Pour one-eighth of the batter and spread into a small round about 4 mm thick.
Cook for 2–3 minutes until the edges set and brown spots appear. Flip and cook another 1–2 minutes until the centre is cooked; use the measured ghee sparingly across the batch.
Serve two warm sweet pudlas per person. They should be tender and lightly caramelized, not as crisp as a plain dosa.
tips: Use a moderate flame because jaggery browns faster than plain batter.
recipe.passiveTime: Rest the wheat-jaggery batter for 15 minutes.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Chakuli Pitha
steps: Wash and soak rice and urad dal separately for 5 hours. Drain and grind with the measured water to a smooth batter slightly thicker than ordinary dosa batter.
Cover loosely and ferment overnight until expanded and bubbly. Fold in salt gently; leave the batter airy instead of beating it flat.
Heat a lightly oiled griddle over medium heat. Pour a ladleful and spread into a medium round, thinner than an uttapam but not paper-thin.
Cover for about 2 minutes until the top shows pores and sets. Flip briefly for 30–45 seconds, keeping the pitha soft with pale golden patches; repeat to make eight.
Serve two warm chakuli pithas per person with coconut chutney. The fermentation and soft texture distinguish them from instant flour crepes.
tips: Let the batter ferment sufficiently; under-fermented batter cooks dense.
recipe.passiveTime: Soak rice and dal for 5 hours; ferment overnight.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Dibba Rotti
steps: Soak urad dal for 4 hours, drain and grind with some measured water to a thick fluffy paste. Rinse rice rava briefly and drain well.
Combine urad paste, rice rava, remaining water, salt, cumin, finely chopped chilli and ginger. Rest 30 minutes so the coarse rice hydrates; the batter should be thick enough to mound.
Heat half the oil in a heavy small pan. Spread half the batter into a thick 2–3 cm disc, cover and cook over very low heat for 12–15 minutes until the bottom forms a deep golden crust.
Drizzle a little oil over the top, flip carefully and cook uncovered for 8–10 minutes until the second side is crusty and the middle cooked. Repeat with the rest of the batter and oil.
Cut each thick rotti into wedges and serve warm with coconut chutney. The crisp outer crust and soft coarse-grained middle are essential.
tips: Do not rush the thick centre over high heat; it needs slow covered cooking.

recipe.name: Ghavan
steps: Whisk fine rice flour, measured water and salt until smooth and thin, without dry lumps. Rest 15 minutes, then stir thoroughly because rice flour settles at the bottom.
Heat a flat seasoned pan on medium-high and brush very lightly with oil. The pan should be hot enough for batter to sizzle but not smoke.
Pour a ladle of thin batter from the outer edge toward the centre, letting it form a lacy crepe. Do not spread forcefully with the ladle or the delicate sheet may tear.
Cover for about 1 minute until the top turns opaque, then uncover and cook 1–2 minutes until the edges lift. Flip only briefly if needed; keep the ghavan mostly soft and pale.
Fold carefully and serve two warm ghavans per person with coconut chutney. Stir the batter before each pour to preserve the thin even texture.
tips: The pan must be hot and the batter thin to make ghavan's lace-like holes.
recipe.passiveTime: Rest the rice-flour batter for 15 minutes.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Amboli
steps: Wash and soak rice, urad dal and fenugreek for 5 hours. Grind with most of the measured water to a smooth thick batter; whisk sorghum flour with the rest of the water and fold it in.
Cover loosely and ferment overnight until the batter rises and develops bubbles. Add salt gently and keep the consistency thick enough for a soft pancake.
Heat a seasoned griddle on medium and brush lightly with oil. Pour a ladle of batter into a thick 12 cm circle without spreading it paper-thin.
Cover for 2–3 minutes until the surface pores open and the top sets. Flip for roughly 1 minute and remove while the amboli is still soft, with light golden patches.
Make eight soft ambolis and serve two per person with coconut chutney. Do not use high heat, which hardens the outside before the middle steams.
tips: A properly fermented thick batter gives amboli its characteristic soft porous top.
recipe.passiveTime: Soak grains for 5 hours and ferment batter overnight.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Chilka Roti
steps: Wash rice and chana dal and soak separately for 4 hours. Drain and grind with measured water into a smooth batter with a little texture from the dal.
Blend in green chilli and ginger, then stir in cumin and salt. The batter should be pourable but thicker than a lacy rice-flour ghavan.
Heat a lightly oiled flat griddle over medium heat. Pour a ladle and spread into a thin round about 15 cm wide.
Cook for 2–3 minutes until the underside is golden and the top sets. Flip and cook 1–2 minutes more until the rice and dal are fully cooked without a raw centre.
Make eight chilka rotis and serve two per person with tomato chutney. Stir the batter before each one so the dal remains evenly mixed.
tips: The rice and chana dal batter is ground fresh; this version does not require overnight fermentation.
recipe.passiveTime: Soak rice and chana dal for 4 hours.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Dhuska
steps: Soak yellow peas overnight. Drain and simmer in fresh water until tender, about 40–60 minutes; reserve 250 ml of their cooking liquid.
Soak rice, chana dal and urad dal for 4 hours, drain and grind with the measured water to a thick smooth batter. Stir in half the salt and rest 15 minutes.

For ghugni, heat 20 ml of the oil, soften chopped onion and ginger, add tomato, cumin and turmeric, and cook until the tomato breaks down. Add peas, reserved liquid and remaining salt; simmer until spoonable.
Heat the remaining oil in a deep pan to about 175°C. Drop a small ladle of batter for each dhuska and fry 2–3 minutes per side until puffed, deep golden and cooked in the centre; drain.
Serve two hot dhuskas per person with a bowl of yellow-pea ghugni and chopped coriander. The fried breads should be crisp outside and soft within.
tips: Fry a test dhuska first; if it spreads flat, the batter is too thin.
recipe.passiveTime: Soak rice and dals for 4 hours; soak dried yellow peas overnight.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Ukadpendi
steps: Dry-roast whole wheat flour over low heat for 7–9 minutes, stirring continuously, until nutty and lightly golden. Spread it on a plate so it stops cooking; do not leave raw-flour patches.
Heat oil in a broad pan, splutter mustard and cumin, then cook finely chopped onion and green chilli until the onion softens. Stir in turmeric and salt.
Bring measured water to a boil in the pan. Lower the heat and sprinkle in the roasted flour gradually while stirring firmly to prevent lumps.
Cover and steam over low heat for 5–7 minutes, stirring once, until the flour is cooked and forms moist small crumbs rather than dry powder or a sticky paste.
Fluff with a fork, add lemon juice and coriander, and divide into four bowls. Serve warm while the crumbly texture is distinct.
tips: Roast the flour thoroughly before adding water; raw flour cannot be fixed after steaming.
recipe.passiveTime: No long resting time required.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Sev Usal
steps: Soak white peas overnight, drain and simmer in fresh water until soft but intact, roughly 40–60 minutes. Reserve 350 ml cooking liquid.
Heat oil in a broad pan, toast cumin, soften half the chopped onion with ginger and garlic, then add tomato, chilli powder, coriander powder, turmeric and salt.
Cook the masala 7–8 minutes until the tomato breaks down. Add cooked peas and reserved liquid and simmer 10 minutes into a spicy spoonable usal; lightly mash a few peas to thicken.
Divide hot usal among four bowls. Add remaining raw onion, fresh coriander and a generous layer of fine sev only just before serving so the topping remains crisp.
Serve with lemon wedges and soft pav, allowing each person to squeeze lemon to taste. Keep the peas visible rather than blending the curry smooth.
tips: Add sev at the last moment or it dissolves into the hot pea gravy.

recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Nagori Halwa
steps: Mix plain flour with 50 g of the semolina, 4 g salt and 20 ml oil. Add just enough of the measured water to knead a firm puri dough; cover and rest for 20 minutes.

Boil potatoes until tender and break them into chunks. Heat 20 ml oil, toast cumin and ginger, cook chopped tomato with turmeric, chilli and remaining salt, then add potato and 200 ml water. Simmer into a spoonable aloo sabzi.
For halwa, roast the remaining semolina in ghee over low heat until aromatic and lightly golden. Boil 350 ml of the measured water with sugar, then add to the roasted semolina slowly while stirring.
Cook the halwa until thick and glossy, about 5 minutes. Toast cashews in a little ghee taken from the measured amount and scatter over the halwa.
Roll the rested dough into 16 small thin discs. Heat the remaining oil to about 175°C and fry each puri briefly on both sides until puffed and lightly golden; drain on a rack.
Serve four crisp mini puris per person with a separate portion of warm halwa and potato sabzi. Keep sweet and savory components distinct on the plate.
tips: Prepare the halwa and potato sabzi before frying the puris so the puris arrive crisp.
recipe.passiveTime: Rest the puri dough for 20 minutes.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

hi.Cook the halwa until thick and glossy, a: हलवा लगभग 5 मिनट गाढ़ा चमकदार होने तक पकाएँ। नापे घी में से थोड़ा लेकर काजू भूनें और हलवे पर डालें।

recipe.name: Bara Ghugni
steps: Soak yellow peas overnight. Drain and simmer in fresh water until tender, about 40–60 minutes, reserving 350 ml cooking liquid for the ghugni.
Soak urad dal for 4 hours, drain well and grind with only the measured water to a thick smooth batter. Beat for 3 minutes until airy and mix in half the salt.

Heat 25 ml of the oil, splutter cumin, then soften half the chopped onion and ginger. Add tomato, turmeric, chilli and remaining salt; cook until thick. Add peas and reserved liquid and simmer 10 minutes.
Heat the remaining oil to about 175°C. Drop small spoonfuls of urad batter and fry 4–5 minutes, turning, until each bara is crisp golden and fully cooked. Drain on a rack.
Divide warm yellow-pea ghugni into four bowls or plates and add two fresh bara to each. Top with remaining finely chopped raw onion and coriander just before serving.
tips: Keep the bara batter thick and airy so the fritters stay light inside.

recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Dahi Bara Aloo Dum
steps: Soak yellow peas overnight and urad dal for 4 hours. Cook drained peas in fresh water until tender, reserving 200 ml liquid; boil potatoes separately until tender, then cut them into chunks.
Grind drained urad dal with measured water to a thick batter and beat until airy. Mix in 4 g salt. Heat most of the oil to about 175°C and fry small spoonfuls for 4–5 minutes until golden; drain.
Soak the hot bara in warm water for 5 minutes, squeeze gently, then arrange in a shallow dish. Whisk curd with 2 g salt and pour over the soft bara; chill briefly while making the curry.

In the remaining 25 ml oil, toast cumin, soften chopped onion and ginger, then cook tomato with chilli, turmeric and the remaining salt until thick. Add potato and a little water and simmer 10 minutes to a rich aloo dum.
Warm the cooked yellow peas with their reserved liquid and a spoonful of the potato masala to make a light ghugni. Do not blend; the peas should remain visible.
Divide yogurt-soaked bara among four plates. Spoon hot aloo dum and a little ghugni over each, finish with coriander and serve promptly so the cool curd and hot curry contrast.
tips: Soaking and squeezing fried bara makes them soft enough to absorb yogurt without becoming oily.

recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Goan Bhaji Pao
steps: Soak dried chickpeas overnight, drain and simmer in fresh water until tender, about 50–70 minutes. Reserve 300 ml cooking liquid; boil potatoes until tender and cube them.
Heat oil in a broad pan, splutter mustard, then soften chopped onion, ginger and garlic over medium heat for 6 minutes.
Add chopped tomato, coriander powder, turmeric, chilli and salt. Cook 7–8 minutes until the tomato thickens and the oil begins to separate.
Fold in chickpeas, cubed potato and reserved chickpea liquid. Simmer 10 minutes, mashing a few potato pieces to make a thick but spoonable bhaji.
Split and warm the Goan pao. Divide the bhaji into four bowls, top with coriander and serve with two pieces of pao and a lime wedge per person.
tips: A moist bhaji needs the reserved chickpea liquid; plain water makes it less flavorful.
recipe.passiveTime: Soak chickpeas overnight.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Bhutte ka Kees
steps: Coarsely grate or pulse the corn, keeping a few kernels whole for texture; finely chop the chilli and ginger.
Warm ghee in a heavy pan. Splutter mustard and cumin, then fry chilli and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add grated corn, turmeric and salt. Stir over medium heat for 7 minutes until the raw aroma fades.
Pour in milk and cook 10–12 minutes, stirring often, until creamy and thick enough to mound on a spoon.
Turn off the heat, stir in lime juice and coriander, and serve warm in four bowls.
tips: Use fresh tender corn; older kernels need a little extra milk.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Lauki Thepla
steps: Squeeze grated bottle gourd lightly, keeping its juice. Mix flour, gourd, yogurt, chopped coriander and chilli, turmeric, cumin, salt and 10 ml oil.
Knead to a soft nonsticky dough, adding retained gourd juice a spoonful at a time only if needed. Rest covered for 15 minutes.
Divide into eight balls. Dust lightly with flour and roll each into a thin 16–18 cm circle.
Cook each on a hot tawa until spots appear, turn, brush with some remaining oil, and cook both sides until golden spots form.
Stack in a clean cloth to keep soft. Serve warm with plain yogurt.
tips: Do not add water before checking the moisture released by the gourd.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

gu.Quantities serve four adults. Check the: માત્રા ચાર પુખ્ત વ્યક્તિઓ માટે છે. દરેક પગલામાં પાકવાના સંકેત તપાસો અને સ્વાદ પ્રમાણે મસાલો ગોઠવો. જૈન યોગ્યતા તમારા પરિવારના સામગ્રીના નિયમો પર આધારિત છે.

gu.Cook each on a hot tawa until spots appe: ગરમ તવા પર ડાઘ પડે ત્યાં સુધી શેકો, પલટી બાકી તેલમાંથી થોડું લગાવો અને બંને બાજુ સોનેરી ડાઘ પડે ત્યાં સુધી શેકો.

recipe.name: Bathua Paratha
steps: Pick and wash bathua leaves thoroughly. Blanch for 2 minutes, drain well, squeeze dry and finely chop.
Combine flour, bathua, minced chilli, cumin and salt. Add water gradually and knead into a smooth soft dough; rest covered for 15 minutes.
Divide into eight balls and roll each into a 17 cm circle, dusting lightly. Fold once and roll again if you prefer layers.
Cook on a medium-hot tawa until small bubbles appear. Flip, brush with a little ghee, flip again and cook until both sides are brown-spotted.
Serve hot with yogurt; cool completely before packing.
tips: Dry the blanched greens well so the parathas do not tear.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

बथुआ चुनकर अच्छी तरह धोएँ। 2 मिनट उबालकर छानें, निचोड़ें और बारीक काटें।

hi.Dry the blanched greens well so the para: उबले पत्ते अच्छी तरह निचोड़ें ताकि पराठे न फटें।

બથુઆના પાન વીણી સારી રીતે ધુઓ. 2 મિનિટ ઉકાળી નિતારી દબાવી પાણી કાઢો અને ઝીણા સમારો.

recipe.name: Cheese Paratha
steps: Knead flour, water and 4 g salt into a soft dough; rest covered for 15 minutes.
Mix grated cheese with minced chilli, chopped coriander and the remaining 3 g salt. Divide into eight portions.
Divide dough into eight balls. Roll each to 10 cm, put one cheese portion in the middle, gather and seal edges, then gently roll to 15 cm.
Cook each on a medium-hot tawa until brown spots appear, turning and brushing with a little ghee on both sides. The cheese must melt and the dough cook through.
Rest 1 minute before cutting; serve warm with yogurt.
tips: Seal tightly and roll gently to stop melted cheese leaking onto the tawa.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Pol Roti
steps: Mix flour, grated coconut, finely chopped onion and chilli, and salt in a bowl.
Add water gradually and knead just until a soft dough forms. Add only enough of the measured water to bind; rest covered for 10 minutes.
Divide into eight pieces. Pat each between lightly oiled hands to a thick 12 cm round; do not roll paper thin.
Cook on a medium-hot dry tawa for 3–4 minutes a side until brown spots form and the center cooks through. Brush lightly with oil near the end.
Serve hot with a vegetarian onion-and-chilli sambol.
tips: Fresh coconut gives the characteristic tender crumb; desiccated coconut needs more water.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Chilre
steps: Whisk buckwheat flour, rice flour and salt together. Add measured water gradually to make a pourable batter without lumps.
Rest the batter for 10 minutes, then stir again; buckwheat settles quickly.
Heat a lightly oiled flat pan over medium heat. Pour one eighth of the batter and tilt or spread thinly into a 17 cm round.
Cook 2 minutes until the surface sets, loosen the edge, flip and cook 1 minute more. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding a little oil each time.
Serve folded with a simple vegetable chutney.
tips: A thin batter makes the lacy edges characteristic of chilre.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Oatmeal Porridge
steps: Bring milk and water to a gentle simmer in a saucepan.
Stir in rolled oats and cinnamon. Cook over low heat for 7–9 minutes, stirring often, until the oats are tender and the porridge is creamy.
Turn off the heat and rest for 2 minutes; add a splash of water if it thickens too much.
Divide into four bowls. Top each with sliced banana, berries and chopped almonds, and serve warm.
tips: Rolled oats keep texture better than instant oats.

recipe.name: Ragi Porridge
steps: Whisk ragi flour into 250 ml cold water until completely smooth; this prevents lumps.
Heat the remaining 200 ml water with milk in a heavy saucepan. Pour in the ragi slurry while whisking continuously.
Cook over low-medium heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring and scraping the base, until the raw flour taste disappears and the porridge thickens.
Turn off the heat. Stir in jaggery and cardamom until dissolved; divide into four bowls and garnish with chopped almonds.
tips: Add jaggery only after switching off the heat to keep the milk smooth.

recipe.name: Bircher Muesli
steps: Mix oats, milk and yogurt in a covered bowl; refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight until the oats soften.
Grate half the apple and toss it with lemon juice to prevent browning. Stir it into the soaked oats.
If the mixture is very thick, loosen with a little milk. Divide among four bowls.
Slice the remaining apple, then top the bowls with apple, chopped almonds and berries. Serve cold.
tips: Add crunchy nuts and fruit only at serving time.
recipe.passiveTime: Chill overnight or for at least 4 hours.

recipe.name: Homemade Granola
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C and line a large baking tray with parchment.
Mix oats, chopped almonds, pumpkin seeds, cinnamon and salt. Pour in maple syrup and oil and stir until everything is coated.
Spread evenly on the tray and press into a thin layer. Bake 25–30 minutes, turning the tray halfway but leaving the clusters mostly undisturbed, until golden.
Cool completely on the tray so the granola crisps, then break into clusters. Store airtight for up to two weeks; serve with yogurt or milk.
tips: Do not judge crispness while warm; it firms as it cools.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Yogurt Parfait
steps: Wash berries and dry them thoroughly; halve any large strawberries.
Spoon one quarter of the yogurt into four clear glasses, then add half the granola and half the berries in even layers.
Add the remaining yogurt, then remaining granola and berries. Drizzle maple syrup evenly over the four glasses.
Serve immediately so the granola stays crisp, or keep the granola separate until serving.
tips: Use unsweetened yogurt to balance the fruit and syrup.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Quinoa Porridge
steps: Rinse quinoa in a fine sieve under cold water for 1 minute to remove bitterness; drain.
Bring quinoa and water to a boil. Cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes until the grains open and most water is absorbed.
Add milk and cinnamon. Cook uncovered 5–7 minutes, stirring, until creamy but individual quinoa grains remain visible.
Divide into four bowls; top with sliced banana, berries and maple syrup. Serve warm.
tips: Rinse well; the natural coating can taste bitter.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Kasha
steps: Rinse the toasted buckwheat groats quickly and drain. Bring measured water and half the salt to a boil.
Add buckwheat, cover and simmer gently for 15–18 minutes until tender and liquid is absorbed. Rest covered 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Meanwhile melt butter in a wide pan and brown chopped onion and sliced mushrooms for 8–10 minutes until their moisture evaporates.
Fold mushrooms into the buckwheat. Season with remaining salt and black pepper, scatter parsley and serve warm in four bowls.
tips: Use whole toasted groats, not buckwheat flour, for a fluffy kasha.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Semolina Porridge
steps: Warm milk and water with salt in a heavy saucepan until steaming but not rapidly boiling.
Rain in semolina slowly while whisking constantly so it does not form lumps.
Cook on low heat for 7–9 minutes, stirring along the base, until smooth and thickened. Stir in sugar and half the butter.
Divide among four bowls; add remaining butter and a spoon of berry jam to each. Serve warm.
tips: Whisk continuously while adding the semolina; lumps are hard to remove later.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Champorado
steps: Rinse glutinous rice briefly. Bring it and measured water to a boil in a heavy pot.
Reduce heat and simmer 20–25 minutes, stirring often, until the rice is very tender and the mixture is thick.
Whisk cocoa with a little hot liquid from the pot until smooth, then stir it back with brown sugar and salt. Cook 3 more minutes.
Spoon into four bowls and drizzle each with milk. Serve warm.
tips: Stir frequently near the end because the sticky rice catches easily.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Bubur Kacang Hijau
steps: Rinse mung beans and soak for 4 hours, then drain. Put them in a pot with measured water, sliced ginger and pandan leaf.
Bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 35–45 minutes until the beans are tender but still whole; stir occasionally.
Remove pandan and ginger. Stir in palm sugar and salt until dissolved, then pour in coconut milk.
Warm gently for 4–5 minutes without a hard boil. Divide into four bowls and serve warm or chilled.
tips: Coconut milk can split at a rolling boil; add it near the end.
recipe.passiveTime: Soak mung beans for 4 hours.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Cheese Grits
steps: Bring water and milk to a gentle boil in a heavy saucepan; add salt.
Whisk in grits in a thin stream. Reduce to low heat and cover loosely.
Cook 20–25 minutes, stirring and scraping the bottom every few minutes, until the grains are tender and creamy.
Turn off the heat and stir in grated cheddar, butter and black pepper. Rest 2 minutes, then divide into four warm bowls.
tips: Use actual coarse corn grits, not cornflour, for the proper texture.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Genfo
steps: Bring measured water and salt to a brisk boil in a sturdy saucepan.
Sprinkle barley flour into the boiling water while stirring vigorously with a strong wooden spoon. Lower the heat.
Stir and fold for 12–15 minutes, scraping the base, until no dry flour remains and the stiff porridge is fully cooked.
Melt butter in a small pan and warm berbere in it for 30 seconds. Mound the genfo on a platter, make a central well and pour in the spiced butter.
Serve immediately, dividing into four portions. Keep extra hot water nearby if the porridge becomes too stiff to stir.
tips: Choose a berbere blend without meat stock or animal ingredients.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Eggless Buttermilk Pancakes
steps: Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk buttermilk with 25 g melted butter, then fold into the dry mix just until no dry flour remains; small lumps are fine. Rest 5 minutes.
Warm a nonstick pan over medium-low heat and brush with some remaining butter. Pour eight small pancakes in batches.
Cook each 2–3 minutes until bubbles appear and the edges set; flip and cook 1–2 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Stack warm pancakes and serve with maple syrup and berries.
tips: Do not overmix; it makes the pancakes tough.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Eggless Crepes
steps: Whisk flour, sugar and salt. Gradually whisk in milk and water to make a smooth, thin batter, then mix in 25 g melted butter.
Rest the batter covered for 20 minutes so the flour hydrates. Stir again; add a spoon of water if it no longer pours thinly.
Heat an 18–20 cm nonstick pan over medium heat and brush with some remaining butter. Pour one eighth of the batter, swirling immediately to coat thinly.
Cook about 90 seconds until the underside is golden, flip carefully and cook 30 seconds more. Repeat for eight crepes.
Fold into quarters and serve with sliced strawberries.
tips: The first crepe tests pan heat; reduce heat if it browns before the top sets.
recipe.passiveTime: Rest batter 20 minutes.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

hi.Fold into quarters and serve with sliced: चार तह में मोड़कर कटी स्ट्रॉबेरी के साथ परोसें।

recipe.name: Buckwheat Galette
steps: Whisk buckwheat flour, half the salt and water into a thin smooth batter. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
Sauté sliced mushrooms in 15 g butter for 6 minutes; add spinach and cook 2 minutes until wilted. Season with remaining salt and pepper.
Heat a lightly buttered 24 cm pan over medium heat. Pour one quarter of the batter and swirl thinly; cook 2 minutes, then flip.
Scatter one quarter of the cheese and mushroom-spinach mixture in the center. Fold four sides inward to form a square, leaving the center visible.
Cook 2 minutes more until cheese melts. Repeat for four galettes, using remaining butter; serve hot.
tips: Buckwheat batter is delicate; turn only after the edges release easily.
recipe.passiveTime: Rest batter 30 minutes.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

hi.Sauté sliced mushrooms in 15 g butter fo: कटे मशरूम 15 ग्राम मक्खन में 6 मिनट भूनें; पालक डालकर 2 मिनट मुरझाने तक पकाएँ। बचे नमक और काली मिर्च से स्वाद दें।

चीज़ पिघलने तक 2 मिनट और पकाएँ। बचे मक्खन से चार गैलेट बनाएँ; गरम परोसें।

recipe.name: Brazilian Tapioca
steps: Use moist, hydrated tapioca starch sold for Brazilian tapioca, or moisten dry tapioca starch gradually until it forms crumbly damp granules; pass through a sieve.
Heat a dry nonstick 20 cm pan over medium-low heat. Sift one quarter of the starch evenly across the base, covering gaps.
Cook 2–3 minutes until the granules bond into a flexible white crepe; do not brown or flip.
Scatter one quarter of the cheese, thin tomato slices, a pinch of salt and oregano on half. Fold over and cook 1 more minute until cheese melts.
Repeat for four crepes and serve immediately while warm and chewy.
tips: Ordinary dry tapioca flour needs hydration and sieving before it will bind in the pan.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

hi.Repeat for four crepes and serve immedia: चार क्रेप ऐसे बनाएँ और गरम तथा चबाने योग्य रहते तुरंत परोसें।

gu.Use moist, hydrated tapioca starch sold: બ્રાઝિલિયન ટેપિયોકા માટે મળતું ભીનું સ્ટાર્ચ લો, અથવા સૂકા સ્ટાર્ચમાં થોડું-થોડું પાણી ઉમેરી ભીના ભૂકા દાણા બનાવો; ચાળી લો.

gu.Repeat for four crepes and serve immedia: આ રીતે ચાર ક્રેપ બનાવી ગરમ અને ચવાય એવા હોય ત્યારે તરત પીરસો.

recipe.name: Cachapas
steps: Pulse corn kernels with milk just until a coarse, spoonable batter forms; leave some kernels intact.
Mix in cornmeal, sugar and salt. Rest 10 minutes so the cornmeal absorbs moisture.
Melt a little butter in a medium-hot pan. Spoon one quarter of the batter into a thick 16 cm round and cook 4–5 minutes until the base is deep golden and the top begins to set.
Flip carefully and cook 3–4 minutes. Add one quarter of the cheese, fold in half and warm 1 minute until the cheese softens. Repeat for four.
Serve hot while the edges are golden and the center remains tender.
tips: Fresh corn provides the sweet flavor and coarse texture; do not puree it smooth.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

hi.Pulse corn kernels with milk just until: मक्के के दाने दूध के साथ थोड़े पल्स करें, जब तक मोटा चम्मच से डालने योग्य घोल बने; कुछ दाने साबुत रखें।
hi.Mix in cornmeal, sugar and salt. Rest 10: मक्के का आटा, चीनी और नमक मिलाएँ। आटा नमी सोखे इसलिए 10 मिनट रखें।
hi.Melt a little butter in a medium-hot pan: मध्यम गरम पैन में थोड़ा मक्खन पिघलाएँ। एक चौथाई घोल 16 सेमी मोटे गोल में डालें और नीचे गहरा सुनहरा तथा ऊपर जमना शुरू होने तक 4–5 मिनट पकाएँ।
hi.Flip carefully and cook 3–4 minutes. Add: सावधानी से पलटकर 3–4 मिनट पकाएँ। एक चौथाई चीज़ डालें, आधा मोड़ें और चीज़ नरम होने तक 1 मिनट गरम करें। चार बनाएँ।
hi.Serve hot while the edges are golden and: किनारे सुनहरे और बीच नरम रहते गरम परोसें।
hi.Fresh corn provides the sweet flavor and: ताज़ा मक्का मिठास और मोटी बनावट देता है; इसे पूरी तरह चिकना न पीसें।

gu.Pulse corn kernels with milk just until: મકાઈના દાણા દૂધ સાથે થોડા પલ્સ કરો, મોટા કણવાળું ચમચીથી રેડી શકાય એવું ખીરું બને ત્યાં સુધી; થોડા દાણા આખા રાખો.
gu.Mix in cornmeal, sugar and salt. Rest 10: મકાઈનો લોટ, ખાંડ અને મીઠું ભેળવો. લોટ ભીનાશ શોષે માટે 10 મિનિટ રાખો.
gu.Melt a little butter in a medium-hot pan: મધ્યમ ગરમ પેનમાં થોડું માખણ ઓગાળો. ખીરાનો ચોથો ભાગ 16 સેમીના જાડા ગોળમાં રેડી 4–5 મિનિટ તળિયું ઘેરું સોનેરી અને ઉપરની સપાટી જામવા લાગે ત્યાં સુધી શેકો.
gu.Flip carefully and cook 3–4 minutes. Add: સાવચેતીથી પલટી 3–4 મિનિટ શેકો. ચોથો ભાગ ચીઝ મૂકી અડધું વાળો અને ચીઝ નરમ થાય ત્યાં સુધી 1 મિનિટ ગરમ કરો. ચાર બનાવો.
gu.Serve hot while the edges are golden and: કિનારી સોનેરી અને મધ્ય ભાગ નરમ હોય ત્યારે ગરમ પીરસો.
gu.Fresh corn provides the sweet flavor and: તાજી મકાઈ મીઠાશ અને મોટા કણની બનાવટ આપે છે; સાવ લીસું ન પીસો.

recipe.name: Baghrir
steps: Blend semolina, flour, warm water, yeast, baking powder, sugar and salt into a smooth pourable batter.
Cover and leave in a warm place for 30–45 minutes until slightly bubbly, then stir gently.
Heat a nonstick pan on medium heat. Pour one eighth of the batter into a 14 cm round. Cook only on one side for 2–3 minutes until many tiny holes form and the surface dries.
Slide off without flipping. Repeat, spacing pancakes so they do not stick while cooling.
Melt butter and mix with jaggery syrup; spoon over the warm baghrir and serve.
tips: Baghrir is traditionally honeyed; this vegetarian version uses jaggery syrup instead.
recipe.passiveTime: Batter rises for 30–45 minutes.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

hi.Quantities serve four adults. Check the: मात्राएँ चार वयस्कों के लिए हैं। हर चरण में पकने के संकेत जाँचें और स्वाद के अनुसार मसाला बदलें। जैन उपयुक्तता आपके परिवार की सामग्री संबंधी नियमों पर निर्भर है।
hi.Blend semolina, flour, warm water, yeast: सूजी, मैदा, गुनगुना पानी, खमीर, बेकिंग पाउडर, चीनी और नमक चिकना बहने वाला घोल बनने तक ब्लेंड करें।
hi.Cover and leave in a warm place for 30–4: ढककर गरम जगह 30–45 मिनट हल्के बुलबुले आने तक रखें, फिर धीरे हिलाएँ।
hi.Heat a nonstick pan on medium heat. Pour: नॉनस्टिक पैन मध्यम आँच पर गरम करें। घोल का आठवाँ भाग 14 सेमी गोल डालें। सिर्फ एक तरफ 2–3 मिनट पकाएँ, जब तक कई छोटे छेद बनें और ऊपर सूख जाए।
hi.Slide off without flipping. Repeat, spac: बिना पलटे उतारें। बाकी बनाएँ और ठंडा होते समय अलग रखें ताकि चिपकें नहीं।
hi.Melt butter and mix with jaggery syrup;: मक्खन पिघलाकर गुड़ की चाशनी मिलाएँ; गरम बाघरीर पर डालकर परोसें।
hi.Baghrir is traditionally honeyed; this v: इस शाकाहारी रूप में शहद के बदले गुड़ की चाशनी है।

gu.Quantities serve four adults. Check the: માત્રા ચાર પુખ્ત વ્યક્તિઓ માટે છે. દરેક પગલામાં પાકવાના સંકેત તપાસો અને સ્વાદ પ્રમાણે મસાલો ગોઠવો. જૈન યોગ્યતા તમારા પરિવારના સામગ્રીના નિયમો પર આધારિત છે.
gu.Blend semolina, flour, warm water, yeast: સોજી, મેંદો, હૂંફાળું પાણી, યીસ્ટ, બેકિંગ પાવડર, ખાંડ અને મીઠું લીસું રેડી શકાય એવું ખીરું થાય ત્યાં સુધી બ્લેન્ડ કરો.
gu.Cover and leave in a warm place for 30–4: ઢાંકી ગરમ જગ્યાએ 30–45 મિનિટ થોડા પરપોટા આવે ત્યાં સુધી રાખો, પછી હળવેથી હલાવો.
gu.Heat a nonstick pan on medium heat. Pour: નોનસ્ટિક પેન મધ્યમ તાપે ગરમ કરો. ખીરાનો આઠમો ભાગ 14 સેમી ગોળ રેડો. માત્ર એક બાજુ 2–3 મિનિટ અનેક નાના છિદ્રો બને અને ઉપર સુકાય ત્યાં સુધી શેકો.
gu.Slide off without flipping. Repeat, spac: પલટ્યા વગર ઉતારો. બાકી બનાવો અને ઠંડા થતાં અલગ રાખો જેથી ચોંટે નહીં.
gu.Melt butter and mix with jaggery syrup;: માખણ ઓગાળી ગોળની ચાસણી ભેળવો; ગરમ બાઘરીર પર રેડી પીરસો.
gu.Baghrir is traditionally honeyed; this v: આ શાકાહારી રૂપમાં મધને બદલે ગોળની ચાસણી છે.

recipe.name: Msemen
steps: Mix flour, 100 g semolina and salt. Add warm water gradually and knead 8–10 minutes into a smooth elastic dough.
Divide into eight balls, lightly oil each and rest covered for 30 minutes.
Mix remaining 60 g semolina with melted butter. On an oiled surface, stretch one ball very thin, brush with some butter mixture and fold all four sides toward the center into a square.
Flatten gently, then cook in a lightly oiled pan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes per side, turning until both sides have brown spots and the layers cook through.
Repeat with the other seven balls and serve warm.
tips: Keep the dough covered during shaping so the thin layers do not dry out.
recipe.passiveTime: Rest dough 30 minutes.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

hi.Quantities serve four adults. Check the: मात्राएँ चार वयस्कों के लिए हैं। हर चरण में पकने के संकेत जाँचें और स्वाद के अनुसार मसाला बदलें। जैन उपयुक्तता आपके परिवार की सामग्री संबंधी नियमों पर निर्भर है।
hi.Mix flour, 100 g semolina and salt. Add: मैदा, 100 ग्राम सूजी और नमक मिलाएँ। गुनगुना पानी धीरे डालकर 8–10 मिनट चिकना लचीला आटा गूँधें।
hi.Divide into eight balls, lightly oil eac: आठ लोइयाँ करें, हर एक पर हल्का तेल लगाएँ और ढककर 30 मिनट रखें।
hi.Mix remaining 60 g semolina with melted: बची 60 ग्राम सूजी को पिघले मक्खन में मिलाएँ। तेल लगी सतह पर एक लोई बहुत पतली फैलाएँ, कुछ मक्खन मिश्रण लगाएँ और चारों तरफ से बीच की ओर मोड़कर चौकोर बनाएँ।
hi.Flatten gently, then cook in a lightly o: धीरे चपटा करके हल्के तेल लगे पैन में मध्यम आँच पर हर तरफ 3–4 मिनट भूरे चित्ते और परतें अंदर तक पकने तक सेंकें।
hi.Repeat with the other seven balls and se: बाकी सात लोइयों से भी ऐसे बनाएँ और गरम परोसें।
hi.Keep the dough covered during shaping so: बेलते समय आटा ढका रखें ताकि पतली परतें न सूखें।

gu.Mix flour, 100 g semolina and salt. Add: મેંદો, 100 ગ્રામ સોજી અને મીઠું ભેળવો. હૂંફાળું પાણી ધીમે ઉમેરી 8–10 મિનિટ લીસો લવચીક લોટ બાંધો.
gu.Divide into eight balls, lightly oil eac: આઠ લૂવા કરો, દરેક પર થોડું તેલ લગાવી ઢાંકી 30 મિનિટ રાખો.
gu.Mix remaining 60 g semolina with melted: બાકી 60 ગ્રામ સોજી ઓગાળેલા માખણમાં ભેળવો. તેલવાળી સપાટી પર એક લૂવો ખૂબ પાતળો ખેંચો, માખણનું મિશ્રણ લગાવી ચારેય બાજુ વચ્ચેથી વાળી ચોરસ બનાવો.
gu.Flatten gently, then cook in a lightly o: હળવેથી સપાટ કરી થોડા તેલવાળા પેનમાં મધ્યમ તાપે દરેક બાજુ 3–4 મિનિટ ભૂરા ડાઘ અને પડ અંદર સુધી પાકે ત્યાં સુધી શેકો.
gu.Repeat with the other seven balls and se: બાકી સાત લૂવા પણ એમ જ બનાવી ગરમ પીરસો.
gu.Keep the dough covered during shaping so: વણતી વખતે લોટ ઢાંકી રાખો જેથી પાતળા પડ સુકાય નહીં.

recipe.name: Bombay Masala Toast
steps: Boil potatoes until tender, peel and mash coarsely. Mix with cumin, chilli powder and 5 g salt.
Spread green chutney on four bread slices. Add one quarter of potato mash to each, then thin tomato and onion slices. Sprinkle remaining salt.
Top with the other four bread slices. Brush the outsides with butter.
Toast in a sandwich press or heavy pan, pressing lightly, for 4–5 minutes per side until crisp with deep grill marks and the filling is hot.
Cut diagonally and serve immediately with extra chutney if desired.
tips: Use a thick green chutney so the bread remains crisp.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

hi.Boil potatoes until tender, peel and mas: आलू नरम होने तक उबालकर छीलें और मोटा मसलें। जीरा, मिर्च पाउडर और 5 ग्राम नमक मिलाएँ।
hi.Spread green chutney on four bread slice: चार ब्रेड स्लाइस पर हरी चटनी लगाएँ। हर एक पर चौथाई आलू, फिर पतले टमाटर और प्याज़ रखें। बचा नमक छिड़कें।
hi.Top with the other four bread slices. Br: बाकी चार ब्रेड स्लाइस ऊपर रखें। बाहर की तरफ मक्खन लगाएँ।
hi.Toast in a sandwich press or heavy pan,: सैंडविच प्रेस या भारी पैन में हल्का दबाते हुए हर ओर 4–5 मिनट गहरी ग्रिल धारियाँ और गरम भरावन होने तक टोस्ट करें।
hi.Cut diagonally and serve immediately wit: तिरछा काटकर तुरंत परोसें; चाहें तो और चटनी दें।
hi.Use a thick green chutney so the bread r: ब्रेड कुरकुरी रखने के लिए गाढ़ी हरी चटनी लें।

gu.Spread green chutney on four bread slice: ચાર બ્રેડ સ્લાઈસ પર લીલી ચટણી લગાવો. દરેક પર ચોથો ભાગ બટાકા, પછી પાતળાં ટામેટાં અને ડુંગળી મૂકો. બાકી મીઠું છાંટો.
gu.Top with the other four bread slices. Br: બાકી ચાર બ્રેડ સ્લાઈસ ઉપર મૂકો. બહાર માખણ લગાવો.
gu.Toast in a sandwich press or heavy pan,: સેન્ડવિચ પ્રેસ અથવા જાડા પેનમાં હળવું દબાવતા દરેક બાજુ 4–5 મિનિટ ઘેરા ગ્રિલ ડાઘ પડે અને ભરાવન ગરમ થાય ત્યાં સુધી શેકો.
gu.Cut diagonally and serve immediately wit: ત્રાંસા કાપી તરત પીરસો; ગમે તો વધુ ચટણી આપો.
gu.Use a thick green chutney so the bread r: બ્રેડ કરકરી રાખવા ઘટ્ટ લીલી ચટણી લો.

recipe.name: Beans on Toast
steps: Heat oil in a saucepan and soften finely chopped onion for 4 minutes.
Add tomato passata, brown sugar, salt and pepper. Simmer 5 minutes, then fold in cooked white beans.
Cook another 5–6 minutes until the sauce coats the beans; stir gently so they remain whole.
Toast four thick bread slices until crisp. Spoon beans generously over the toast, scatter parsley and serve immediately.

recipe.name: Mushrooms on Toast
steps: Wipe mushrooms clean and slice thickly. Toast four slices of sourdough until crisp.
Heat olive oil and half the butter in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms in one layer and leave undisturbed 3 minutes to brown.
Stir, add minced garlic and thyme, and cook 3–4 minutes until moisture evaporates. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread remaining butter on the hot toast, heap mushrooms on top and finish with chopped parsley. Serve at once.
tips: Do not crowd the pan; mushrooms steam instead of browning.
